title: The Roof (Pete McIvor)
style: country blues acoustic guitar warm baritone male vocal storytelling 102bpm walking bass brushed drums honest character portrait unhurried
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Pete was up before the birds
Hammer in his hand, didn't need the words
Twenty years of rooftops, rain or shine
Oldest son, he held the family line

[Verse 2]
Tiles and timber, heat on his back
Didn't need a blueprint, knew the knack
Every house he touched still standing true
That's the kind of man that Pete is through

[Chorus]
From the roof he could see everything
The hills, the river, where the sea begins
And maybe that's the moment, maybe that's the call
When you've been that high, you don't stop at all

[Bridge]
Chas would say — that's the boy, that's the one
Always knew he'd find his way back to the sun

[Verse 3]
Hung up the tool belt, walked toward the tide
Couldn't explain it much, just felt it inside
Now he's on the water, boats and morning air
You wouldn't know it, but the rooftop's still there

[Outro]
The roof is still there
The roof is still there
That's my boy
